# resolveFallbacks turns a malformed fallbackTarget into a valid one

## Context

This was raised in [@neo-gemini-julia's review of #19995](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19995#pullrequestreview-5613827089) (challenge 1). `Placement.resolveFallbacks`, added there for #19993, runs before the topology validation in `Placement#prepare`. Its own comment says that a malformed hint passes through to its errors unchanged, but it does not.

I measured it on `dev` with a scratch probe that calls the real `resolveFallbacks` and `Persistence.captureTopologyPerspective` on a live workspace:

| `fallbackTarget` on a live workspace | validation errors | errors after `resolveFallbacks` |
|---|---|---|
| `nodeId: ''` | requires a non-empty nodeId | none (target → root) |
| `nodeId: '  '` | requires a non-empty nodeId | none |
| no `nodeId` | requires a non-empty nodeId | none |
| `nodeId: 42` | requires a non-empty nodeId | none |
| stale `nodeId` plus a `windowId` field | unexpected field "windowId"; node does not exist | none (field dropped) |
| stale `nodeId` (control) | node does not exist | none (intended) |

## The Problem

`prepare()` is the placement participant's write boundary: every commit that carries placement hints passes through it. A malformed target comes out as a valid one that points at the workspace root, so the write is accepted instead of refused. No shipped writer produces such a target today, because minted hints come from `relativeHint()` and stored ones were validated. The break is in the boundary's contract, and it lets a writer the boundary does not control, such as a programmatic or agent-driven commit, slip past validation.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/dashboard/dock/window/Placement.mjs`, `resolveFallbacks`: it re-targets whenever `document && !Object.hasOwn(document.nodes, target.nodeId)`, and it rebuilds the target as `{workspaceKey, nodeId: document.root}`.
- `src/dashboard/dock/model/Persistence.mjs`, placement-hint validation: it refuses a `nodeId` that is not a non-blank string, and any field outside `fallbackTargetKeys`.
- Design authority: the method's own comment, "Runs before validation: a malformed hint passes through to its errors unchanged."

## The Fix

Re-target only a well-formed target. The check is `typeof nodeId === 'string' && nodeId.trim()`, the same predicate validation applies, plus a node the document lacks. Spread the target (`{...target, nodeId: document.root}`) so that its other fields still reach validation.

Julia's second observation was that reading `hints` after Group retirement now throws. It needs no change. Placement is the only `groupRetired` listener, and `TopologyLibrary#retireIfHeadless` disposes the Workspace synchronously right after `retireGroup`. Neither Workspace's teardown captures the topology, so nothing reads the hints in between.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unit (`test/playwright/unit/dashboard/DockPlacement.spec.mjs`): for an empty, blank, missing or non-string `nodeId` on a live workspace, `resolveFallbacks` returns the hints unchanged and `prepare` refuses with the non-empty-nodeId error. A stale target that carries an extra field is refused for that field. The arm is red on `dev` and green with the fix.
- [ ] The existing stale-fallback arms stay green: "a document commit that removes the fallback node leaves the hints capturable, and undo restores the target" and "a popup move after the fallback node is gone still records its row".

## Out of Scope

- Validation itself (`Persistence`): unchanged.
- Reading `hints` after Group retirement (see The Fix).

## Related

- #19993, #19995: introduced `resolveFallbacks`.
